rv.q: “Assassins” is always hard to watch, and yet usually worth the effort.
If you have yet to fall for it, Theo’s production will light the fuse.
All of this is on display in Theo's fun and fascinating exploration of what has been called "the dark side of the American dream."
Couldn’t ask for anything more from an evening of entertainment.
Speaking for myself, I haven’t stopped picking at the scab where Theo’s production grazed me.
A lovely score, a fresh look at American history plus the sheer artistry of this production are reasons enough to see Theo Ubique’s latest offering.
Theo showed me that they are not afraid to attempt anything and then proved they could with this production of "Assassins".

cn.t: Theo's intimate production of Sondheim's darkest musical earns strong praise for its provocative power and musical talent. Critics find it wickedly funny, disturbingly timely, and captivatingly performed, though note its controversial subject matter won't be for everyone.
